hints.content: In order to find $H'(4)$, we should first find an expression for $H'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $f$, $h$, and their derivatives.

So $H'(x)=f'\Bigl(h(x)\Bigr)\cdot h'(x)$.

We can now plug $x=4$ into this expression and evaluate. Here is the table of values again, for your convenience:

$x$ | $f(x)$ | $h(x)$ | $f'(x)$ | $h'(x)$
:-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
$-2$ | $12$ | $-7$ | $28$ | $-11$
$4$ | $6$ | $-2$ | $5$ | $1$

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
H'(4)&=f'\Bigl(h(4)\Bigr)\cdot h'(4)
\\\\
&=f'(-2)\cdot 1&&\gray{h(4)=-2\text{ , }h'(4)=1}
\\\\
&=28\cdot 1&&\gray{f'(-2)=28}
\\\\
&=28
\end{align}$
